# Angular Internationalization

## Purpose
Define how Angular projects in this ecosystem implement localization, locale parity, and translation completion.

## Scope
Angular projects with more than one supported locale (or expected future locale).

## Load Conditions
Project manifest declares an Angular stack and more than one locale.

## Do Not Load When
Single-locale Angular projects with no foreseeable localization requirement.

## Rules
- The project MUST declare a single canonical locale type as the source of truth for required locale coverage (e.g. `AppLocale` exported from `src/app/core/i18n/i18n.types.ts`).
- Translations MUST live in one centralized translation source (e.g. `src/app/core/i18n/i18n.translations.ts`) — not scattered JSON files unless the project's `project.manifest.md` explicitly declares an alternate strategy.
- Translation resolution MUST be implemented through one i18n service + one translation pipe (e.g. `i18n.service.ts` + `translate.pipe.ts`). Do not duplicate translation pipes per feature.
- MUST use stable translation keys by feature/scope/intent.
- MUST NOT hardcode user-facing strings in templates, screens, dialogs, forms, tables, services that produce UI copy.
- MUST keep pluralization and formatting locale-aware.
- MUST NOT mix languages in the same UI path.
- Translation entries MUST stay structurally consistent across all locales declared by the canonical locale type.
- Missing translations MUST fail visibly during development.
- Locale metadata MUST be centralized in the i18n types file.

## Mandatory workflow
When creating/modifying user-facing UI: reuse an existing key if it exists; otherwise define a stable semantic key; use the key in HTML/TS instead of raw text; update the translation source in the same task; add the entry for every locale in the canonical locale type; preserve the same semantic key tree across locales; verify no unresolved key reaches the rendered UI.

## Completion rule
A task is NOT complete if user-facing text was introduced but not translated, a key is referenced from UI but missing from the translation source, a key exists for one locale but not all, locale trees drift structurally, or unresolved keys can reach the rendered UI.

## Output Expectations
- Locales evolve by extending the canonical locale type and the translation source — no folder restructuring.
- Every locale renders the same UI shape.
- Missing translations are caught at development time.
